content.title: About
content.content: Fruit punch is a refreshing beverage made from fruit juices mixed with carbonated water. It combines the natural sweetness of fruits with a light fizz, creating a bright flavor suitable for both children and adults.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first fruit punch appeared in the United States in the early 1920s.
Blending different juices (orange, pineapple, cherry) provides a variety of taste notes.
Carbonated water helps quench thirst more quickly.
Punch is often served at parties and summer cafés as a non‑alcoholic alternative.

items.title: Vitamin boost
items.content: Fresh fruit juice is rich in vitamin C and other antioxidants that support the immune system.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Carbonated water contributes to rapid fluid replenishment.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The drink contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Fruit juices provide potassium, magnesium, and small amounts of calcium, beneficial for heart and muscle function.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some versions may contain added sugar, increasing the calorie count.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity of fruit juices can irritate the stomach in people with gastritis.

items.title: Carbonation
items.content: The fizz may cause bloating in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve fruit punch chilled in glasses or cups. Garnish with fruit slices, mint leaves, or ice cubes. It works as a standalone drink or as a base for non‑alcoholic cocktails.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared punch in the refrigerator in a sealed container for no more than 3‑4 days. For longer storage, keep the carbonated water separate from the juice to preserve fizz.
